newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends firmer amid listless trade.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends firmer amid listless trade.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures ended a sluggish session slightly higher on Friday, still in a consolidation mode.
July closed up four stg at 1,010 stg per tonne. September also gained three to 1,025. But total volume was a lackluster 3,117 contracts.
Scattered outright activity made up most of the volume, but traders said most of the trades came in 100 to 300 lots at a time. They speculated most of the activity was tidying up before the weekend.
Though July edged up to the highest level since April 29, traders said volume was too thin to read much into the move.

They said speculators in London were probably flat to slightly net short. But they said new York speculators were probably very long. Some predicted the CFTC commitment of traders report, due in New York later in the day, would show speculators long 12,000 to 18,000 lots.
Some said if July stays firm and can build a solid base near current levels, the market may try to test the upside again.
A fund trader said the upcoming months were also seasonally favourable for cocoa. Historically, cocoa has rallied around this time of year, he said.
But traders stressed that if July slipped below the April 9 low of 980, all bullish forecasts would be erased and July could quickly fall into the 930- to 920-area.

Though sterling has moved around a lot this week, traders said they saw little arbitrage-related activity. They said some arbitrage surfaced earlier in the week when sterling was closer to $1.63. But at current levels closer to $1.62, they said very little was happening against New York.
They said traders had positions against New York but not through arbitraging.

Traders attributed the low liquidity to lack of fresh fundamental news, unclear technicals and fears of setting positions in September because of what a major trade house believed to be holding a large cocoa position could do with its stockpile. As a result, most activity in September has been confined to trade buying.
While volume in nearby months have tapered off, back months have generally seen more action. They said industry bought December/March while trade sold this week.
December/March has narrowed this week from about 15 stg to 11 at the close and eight earlier, traders said.
